title: No check feeds NaN to score_lead_predictions; dropping its guard poisons lead sigma permanently
claim: Disabling accuracy.py:261 (`if not np.isfinite(actual_temp): return` -> `if False:`) survives all 20 drivers of accuracy.py's measured closure (12 run, 8 reach-skipped; env_drift.py --all against the baseline included), yet on one NaN reading it turns AccuracyTracker.sigma(3.0) from 0.5 to nan and keeps it nan after a later finite scoring.
mechanism: lead_sigma is an EWMA: (1-a)*prev + a*err, so one NaN err makes every later value NaN; the guard is the only barrier inside the tracker, and no test drives a non-finite actual_temp into it.

evidence.contention_note: deterministic; survivor verdict from drive_resumable.py (tally.py: accuracy.py:261 GUARD_OFF LIVES), box shared with D0-s2 and D9-s2 at load ~7

null_control.note: null mutant: baseline and mutant sigma both 0.5; the sibling guard accuracy.py:238 (non-finite predicted) reads 0 too: it is shadowed by the loop's own isfinite(predicted) filter, an equivalent survivor

metric_definition: 1 when AccuracyTracker.sigma(3.0) after a NaN then a finite scoring differs between the baseline module and the in-memory mutant, else 0
phenomenon_property: Every non-finite guard at a learner's state boundary in the cells has a check that feeds it a non-finite value and asserts the learned state stays finite.
proposed_fix_scope: Test only: one check (features.py or a unit block) scoring a NaN actual_temp after a finite one and asserting sigma stays finite and lead_counts unchanged; then pin the site killed_by.
